# Code of Conduct

## Our commitment

DupeLens welcomes people of every background and experience level. Everyone taking part deserves a respectful environment, regardless of age, disability, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, nationality, appearance, race, religion, sexual orientation, or technical experience.

This policy applies to issues, pull requests, reviews, discussions, other project spaces, and people representing DupeLens elsewhere.

## Expected behavior

- Be considerate, patient, and constructive. Ask questions rather than assuming intent.
- Critique the work and its tradeoffs, not the person who contributed it.
- Respect different experiences and give newcomers room to learn.
- Accept corrections, acknowledge mistakes, and help resolve disagreements.
- Respect other people's privacy, time, and boundaries.
- Use project spaces for relevant, good-faith collaboration.

## Unacceptable behavior

- Harassment, threats, intimidation, stalking, or discriminatory language.
- Sexualized language or imagery, unwanted sexual attention, or advances.
- Personal attacks, deliberate humiliation, sustained disruption, or targeted provocation.
- Publishing private information without permission, including private correspondence.
- Retaliation against someone who reports a concern or assists an investigation.
- Continuing unwanted contact after being asked to stop.

Technical disagreement and respectful criticism are welcome. They do not excuse abusive behavior.

## Reporting concerns

Email **muhammadtalhabinkhalid@gmail.com** with the subject **DupeLens conduct report**. Include relevant links, what happened, when it happened, and immediate concerns. Share only information needed to understand the report. Do not post sensitive details in a public issue.

Reports are handled by the maintainer, [@illusionoftalha](https://github.com/illusionoftalha), and treated as confidential where practical. Information may need to be shared with people necessary to investigate or act on a concern; absolute confidentiality cannot be guaranteed.

If the concern involves the maintainer, you may also use [GitHub's reporting channels](https://support.github.com/contact/report-abuse) for conduct on GitHub. That process is separate from project enforcement.

## Enforcement

The maintainer may remove content, limit participation, close discussions, or block accounts to protect the community. Responses depend on seriousness, impact, and patterns of behavior and may include a correction request, a private warning, a temporary restriction, or a permanent ban.

A warning is not required before action on severe misconduct. When practical, the affected person will receive an explanation and an opportunity to respond privately. Requests for reconsideration can be sent to the reporting email with relevant new information. Enforcement should be proportionate and consistent; contribution history does not exempt anyone from this policy.
